title: Two systems of distinct representatives whose images are disjoint glue into one on the union of their index sets, with no disjointness required of the index sets themselves
statement: Let nb be a family of finite sets of naturals, and let f be a system of distinct representatives for nb on the index set s1 and g one on s2 -- each picks a member of nb i for every index i in its own set, injectively. If the two images never meet (f a is never equal to g b for a in s1 and b in s2), then the function that takes f's value on s1 and g's value elsewhere is a system of distinct representatives for nb on the union of s1 and s2. The index sets need NOT be disjoint: the glued function reads s1 first, so a shared index takes f's value and the definition is unambiguous with no side condition. This is a kernel term with an empty axiom footprint.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Hall.isMatching_union : ((x0 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x1 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat.Finset)) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x5 : AxNat.Hall.IsMatching x0 x2 x3) -> ((x6 : AxNat.Hall.IsMatching x1 x2 x4) -> ((x7 : ((x7 : AxNat) -> ((x8 : AxNat) -> ((x9 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x7) Bool.true) -> ((x10 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x1 x8) Bool.true) -> ((x11 : Eq.{1} AxNat (x3 x7) (x4 x8)) -> False)))))) -> AxNat.Hall.IsMatching (AxNat.Finset.union x0 x1) x2 (AxNat.Hall.glue x3 x4 x0)))))))))
formal.kernel_statement: Nat.Hall.glue f g s := fun i => Bool.rec (motive := fun _ => Nat) (g i) (f i) (Nat.Finset.memB s i); Nat.Hall.IsMatching s nb f := And (forall i, memB s i = true -> memB (nb i) (f i) = true) (forall i j, memB s i = true -> memB s j = true -> Eq Nat (f i) (f j) -> Eq Nat i j). The union membership law the mixed branches consume is Nat.Finset.memB_union_elim : forall s t i, Eq Bool (memB (union s t) i) true -> Or (Eq Bool (memB s i) true) (Eq Bool (memB t i) true).

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `hall-counting`, roadmap item W2-12 residue: `nat_prelude/hall.rs` gains `glue` and `isMatching_union`; `nat_prelude/finset.rs` gains the union's membership calculus (`memB_union`, `memB_union_left`, `memB_union_right`, `memB_union_elim`). ADR-1623.
provenance.source: The combining step of the standard inductive proof of Hall's marriage theorem, where two matchings produced by the inductive hypothesis on two smaller families are assembled into one.

prior_art.establishes: the same gluing of two injective partial functions, stated over `Set`/`Finset` with decidable membership from a typeclass; that route requires the domains to be disjoint (or supplies an agreement hypothesis on the overlap), where this one reads the left set first and needs neither

evidence.supports: two matchings with disjoint images glue into a matching on the union of their index sets
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: ADR-1614 expected Nat.Finset.card_le_of_injOn to be the tool. It is not: that lemma COUNTS an injection, and what is needed here is that the glued function IS one. The content is four branches, one per pair of decisions on `memB s1 i` and `memB s1 j`; the two diagonal ones are each matching's own injectivity and the two mixed ones are refuted by the disjointness hypothesis at exactly that pair, reached through memB_union_elim ('in the union but not in s1' gives 'in s2'). Requiring disjoint INDEX sets would have cost every consumer an obligation the argument never uses.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The same proof term offered with the disjoint-images hypothesis DROPPED must be REJECTED by the trusted gate. That statement is false -- two matchings whose images collide do not glue into an injective function -- and the control differs from the theorem by exactly one binder.

evidence.supports: a member of a union of finite sets is a member of one of them
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: Produces an `Or` rather than a computed index deliberately: the two sides may overlap, and `setUnion` reads the left one first, so the decision on `memB s i` IS the disjunction. Its pointwise base `memB_union` costs one step more than the difference's, because `union` stores `bound s + bound t` and putting an index above it means putting it above EACH -- le_add_right on the left, the same lemma plus one add_comm on the right. `memB_union_right` needs a decision on `memB s i` where its `_left` twin needs none, for the same left-first reason.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The same proof term offered with `And` in place of `Or` must be REJECTED: a member of the union need not be in both sides, so that statement is FALSE rather than merely unprovable here.

evidence.supports: the glue takes f on the set and g off it, and not the other way round
evidence.notes: Nat.Hall.glue is a Definition, so the trusted gate cannot tell you it is wrong -- a glue reading the selector the other way round has exactly the same type. It is reduced at concrete arguments with the wrong formula named: with f i = i + 10, g i = i + 20 and s = {1}, the glue is 11 at 1 and 22 at 2, and the swapped convention's answers 21 and 12 are named as the values it must NOT produce. A mutation exchanging the two branches WAS run: it killed all 18 tests in the module by making the shared prelude unbuildable, because the proof terms name the selector's branches positionally through select_nat_true/select_nat_false. So this test is the readable pin on the convention, not a load-bearing guard -- ADR-1623's mutation table records that this lane predicted otherwise and the measurement refuted it.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Every Nat assertion names the value the swapped convention would produce, and the test additionally requires the two glued values to be distinct -- the property the injectivity branch of isMatching_union needs the disjoint-images hypothesis for.

evidence.notes: The presence check is not decoration: Kernel::axiom_footprint returns an EMPTY vector for a name that was never declared, so a footprint assertion alone passes vacuously on a typo'd or missing declaration. Environment::contains is what makes the exit status depend on the finding. The shape_search binary was rebuilt at this lane's HEAD (declarations=3017, up from 3000 at the base commit, the increment being exactly the seventeen new declarations), and the freshness control postdates every commit in the lane, so a stale index cannot pass.

notes:
epistemic_status and external_status agree on purpose: gluing two injective partial functions with disjoint images is not a new mathematical result. Two things here are worth the ledger entry. First, the statement is STRONGER than the textbook's in one place -- no disjointness of index sets -- and that strength is a consequence of computing the carrier rather than extracting it, since the glue can read a decidable membership instead of needing an agreement hypothesis on the overlap. Second, it closes the last of ADR-1614's three named obstructions on Hall's sufficiency.

Hall's marriage theorem in the SUFFICIENCY direction is still NOT proved, and nat_prelude::hall_tests::hall_necessity_is_admitted_and_sufficiency_is_not pins that in both directions with the same proof term. Nothing in this fact is a matching-EXISTENCE result: both matchings are given.
